title: CPCB AQI Scale (India)
content: India's CPCB AQI scale: 0-50 Good; 51-100 Satisfactory; 101-200 Moderate; 201-300 Poor; 301-400 Very Poor; 401-500+ Severe. Values above 200 warrant health advisories.

title: NDVI Interpretation
content: NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) ranges from -1 to +1. Values near 0 to negative indicate water or built-up areas. Values 0.2 to 0.5 indicate sparse vegetation. Values above 0.5 indicate dense, healthy vegetation.

title: NDWI Interpretation
content: NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index) is used to monitor changes related to water content. Positive values generally represent water bodies, while negative values represent soil and vegetation.

title: Water Health Spectral Proxies
content: Water Health combines detected-water applicability from MNDWI with algal/chlorophyll-related NDCI and relative turbidity/suspended-material spectral signals. These are remote-sensing indicators, not laboratory chlorophyll or NTU measurements, and temporal changes are interpreted as potential indicators rather than causal proof.

title: LST and Urban Heat
content: LST (Land Surface Temperature) measures the temperature of the ground. Elevated LST compared to surrounding areas often indicates an Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, associated with dense built environments and lack of vegetation.

title: Isolation Forest Anomalies
content: Isolation Forest identifies spatial anomalies by isolating data points. An anomalous zone has an environmental profile statistically distinct from the broader city-wide spatial snapshot at that point in time.

title: Mumbai Monsoon Impact
content: Mumbai experiences intense monsoon rainfall from June to September. During this period, optical satellite imagery (like Landsat LST) is often obscured by persistent cloud cover, leading to unavailable data. Rain also washes out atmospheric particulate matter, frequently resulting in unusually low (Good) AQI readings.
